snip.t: Refers to a form of DPLD characterized by evidence of Usual Interstitial Pneumonia
*Honeycomb lung with fibroblast foci and a "usual interstitial pneumonia" pattern is the classic diagnostic combination for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.*
Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF): A chronic, progressive interstitial lung disease of unknown etiology characterized by Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP) pattern.
The histologic and radiologic pattern required for diagnosis is Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP).
Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP): The histologic pattern required for the diagnosis of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF), characterized by patchy fibrosis with temporal heterogeneity.
Who: over 50 years, male, smokers; chronic, progressive fibrosis with usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern; unknown cause.

HRCT: subpleural basal reticulation with honey‑comb cysts and traction bronchiectasis: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern – diagnostic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in the appropriate clinical context
The finding on CT of a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern clarifies the diagnosis.

es.q: A lung biopsy is performed on a patient presenting with progressive dyspnea. The histological pattern observed is Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP), characterized by patchy fibrosis with temporal heterogeneity. What is the diagnosis typically associated with this pattern, and what is its prognosis?
es.m: The histologic pattern of Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP) is the pattern required for the diagnosis of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF). IPF has a very poor prognosis, with a mean survival of 3 years or less.

faq.a: Basal subpleural reticulation with honey‑combing and traction bronchiectasis.
faq.q: What is the hallmark HRCT finding in UIP?

faq.a: They slow the rate of FVC decline and improve survival by targeting fibroblast activity.
faq.q: Why are antifibrotics used in UIP?

faq.a: No; it is a progressive disease, but treatment can slow progression and improve quality of life.

exam: What is the most specific imaging finding that confirms UIP? — Basal subpleural honey‑combing on HRCT; absence of ground‑glass opacities.
A 58‑year‑old man with progressive dyspnoea has a restrictive PFT pattern and DLCO 40% predicted. What is the next best step? — High‑resolution CT to look for UIP pattern.
Why is a normal BAL not sufficient to rule out infection in a patient with suspected UIP? — BAL may miss focal infections; clinical correlation and imaging are needed.
Which drug is contraindicated in a patient with significant liver dysfunction and UIP? — Pirfenidone, due to hepatotoxicity.
What clinical sign suggests the patient is developing pulmonary hypertension? — Peripheral oedema and jugular venous distension.

In a low‑resource setting where HRCT is unavailable, which investigation can still support a diagnosis of UIP? — Chest X‑ray showing basal reticular infiltrates combined with a restrictive PFT pattern.
ai.title: Usual Interstitial Pneumonia
ai.subject: Medicine
ai.summary: UIP is the histologic pattern that defines idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. It presents as a chronic, progressive cough and dyspnoea in older smokers, with characteristic HRCT findings of basal subpleural reticulation and honey‑combing.

b: Histology: patchy fibrosis, fibroblast foci, temporal heterogeneity
HRCT: basal subpleural reticulation, honey‑combing, traction bronchiectasis
sections.p: UIP is a histologic pattern of patchy fibrosis with temporal heterogeneity, seen in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and other interstitial lung diseases. Diagnosis requires compatible clinical context and HRCT showing basal subpleural reticulation, honey‑combing and traction bronchiectasis.
